invariant: A card handed to a harness becomes exactly one prompt, assembled from the card, the previous stage's handoff and the card's references — deterministically, from a versioned shape, so the two planes can disagree in a test rather than in an agent's behaviour.
why: Nothing wrote this down before. The bridge spike sent `work.card.title` as the whole prompt (apps/bridge/spike/src/bridge.ts) — the spec, the handoff and every reference were dropped on the floor, and an agent given only a title does the wrong work confidently. That is invisible in every test that asserts the seam 'carries the work'.

The three inputs are exactly what an agent token can read: `GET /v1/boards/:boardId/runs/:runId` returns `{run, card, stage, handoff, references}` and nothing else. So the prompt contract is the whole agent-visible surface, projected into text.
It is versioned because changing how a card reads changes what agents do. A renderer that silently gains a section changes every run on every board; a version in the shape makes that a decision.
grammarSource: kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts:145-161 — RunContext {run, card, stage, handoff, references}
kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts:68-84 — CardView {id, title, spec, currentStageKey, state, attemptCount, ...}
kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts:30-40 — StageDef {key, name, order, ownerKind, owner, gate, wipLimit, routing}
kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts:227-242 — ReferenceView {id, cardId, url, title, subtitle, provider, sourceType, ...}

kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts:1505-1512 — a `request_changes` gate decision merges `{feedback}` into the card's existing handoff, which is why `feedback` is the one handoff key this contract renders specially
agentpod packages/contract/src/card-prompt.ts — CardPrompt + renderCardPrompt, the validator and renderer this corpus drives
renderingRules: Section order is fixed and never depends on the data: title, provenance line, Task, Review feedback, Handoff, References, Completing this card.

An absent section is omitted entirely rather than rendered empty — a heading with nothing under it reads to a harness as 'there was nothing to do here', which is a different claim from 'this was not provided'.
A string `spec` or `handoff` is rendered verbatim (trimmed); anything else is pretty-printed JSON in a fenced block. A harness must never be shown `[object Object]`.
`feedback` on a handoff is lifted out and rendered above the rest of the handoff, because it is a human telling the agent what to change and is the reason the card came back.
The provenance line always states the attempt number. Attempt 2 of a card is not the same instruction as attempt 1, and a harness that cannot tell them apart cannot behave differently on a retry.
The prompt never contains a credential, a lease epoch or an AgentPod id: it crosses into a harness process, and the harness has no use for any of them.

cases.name: rework_after_request_changes
cases.why: THE CASE THAT EARNS THE CONTRACT. A `request_changes` gate decision merges `{feedback}` into the handoff the agent itself produced and re-queues the card. Rendered as an undifferentiated JSON blob, a reviewer's instruction sits below the agent's own summary of what it already did — so the most important sentence on the card is the least prominent. It is lifted out.

cases.name: unversioned
cases.why: A prompt with no version cannot be told from a prompt built by a renderer that predates a section. The version is the whole point of writing the contract down.

cases.name: future_version
cases.why: A hub must refuse a version it cannot render rather than render it as though it were v1. Accepting an unknown version is how a section silently goes missing on one side of the seam.

cases.name: empty_title
cases.why: The title is the one field always rendered and is the harness's whole instruction when there is no spec. An empty one produces a prompt that asks for nothing and gets a confident answer anyway.

cases.name: attempt_zero
cases.why: kaambaan's `attemptCount` increments on claim, so the agent working a card is always on attempt 1 or later (spike finding RQ4). A zero means the count was read from the wrong field, and 'attempt 0' invites a harness to treat a retry as a first run.

cases.name: external_run_id_from_agentpods_own_space
cases.why: The same rule `Run.externalRunId` carries, applied where the id enters rather than where it is stored. An `attempt_…` here means AgentPod's own key was passed off as the board's work run, and the prompt would be built for a run no board has.

cases.name: no_source
cases.why: Mirrors the `externalRunId`/`externalSource` pairing on acp_runs: a prompt built from work whose orchestrator is unnamed cannot be traced back to the board that asked for it, and `externalSource` is deliberately open so the id's shape cannot supply the answer.
